descriptionChirho: That which is possessed or inherited, especially landed property granted by God or held as a hereditary right. Used frequently of territorial possession in Deuteronomy (Deut 2:5 I have given Mount Seir to Esau as a possession; 2:9 I have given Ar to the sons of Lot as a possession; 2:12, 19), of Israel's inheritance of the land (Josh 1:15; 12:6-7), of tribal allotments (Judg 21:17 inheritance of the survivors of Benjamin), and in prophetic/poetic contexts (Ps 61:5 the inheritance of those who fear your name; Jer 32:8 the right of inheritance). Appears with various possessive suffixes (his possession Deut 2:12; 3:20; your possession 2 Chr 20:11; Josh 1:15) and prepositional combinations -- all inflectional variants of the same core meaning.
